title: Support Operations Analysis Report
executive_summary: Analysis of 220 support tickets reveals a total labor cost of $17,445.07 and a mean resolution time of 75.7 minutes. Team Beta carries the highest labor cost share. Chat is the slowest channel by resolution time. Email tickets reopen at a rate more than twice that of chat tickets, and a small high-cost, low-satisfaction segment warrants targeted intervention. Agent workload is moderately concentrated, with the busiest agent handling 7.3% of all tickets.

key_findings.statement: The dataset contains 220 tickets with a mean resolution time of 75.7 minutes and a total labor cost of $17,445.07.
Team Beta incurred the highest labor cost at $6,928.72, followed by Gamma at $5,911.44 and Alpha at $4,604.91. Beta accounts for the largest share of total spend.
Chat had the longest mean resolution time at 82.2 minutes, followed by phone at 74.1 minutes and email at 71.7 minutes.
Email tickets reopen at 15.2%, compared to 6.8% for chat — an increase of 122.5% relative to the chat rate, indicating email interactions are substantially more likely to require follow-up.
Nine tickets meet the high-cost (≥$100) and low-satisfaction (≤2) criteria, with 11.1% of them having been reopened — a segment meriting priority review.

Resolution time has a median of 65.0 minutes and a standard deviation of 51.3 minutes, indicating notable spread. Mean satisfaction (where recorded) is 4.1 out of 5, with 14 tickets missing a satisfaction score.
Tickets were handled by 18 distinct agents. The busiest single agent handled 16 tickets, representing 7.3% of total volume — a moderate but watchable concentration.

limitations: Both the cleaning and analysis pipeline stages reported validation failures; results should be treated as provisional until the underlying data quality issues are investigated and resolved.
Fourteen tickets are missing satisfaction scores, which may introduce bias into the satisfaction mean if missingness is non-random.
The high-cost, low-satisfaction segment contains only 9 tickets, making percentage-based conclusions (e.g., reopen rate) statistically fragile.
Agent identity is based on agent_id only; if agents share IDs or IDs changed over time, concentration metrics may be understated or overstated.
No time-period metadata is reported, so trends over time cannot be assessed from this snapshot.
conclusion: Support operations show acceptable average satisfaction (4.1/5) but meaningful variation in resolution speed and a concerning email reopen rate 122% higher than chat. Team Beta drives the largest labor cost share. Priority actions should include investigating email resolution quality and reviewing the nine high-cost, low-satisfaction tickets. Data pipeline failures must be remediated before these findings are used for formal decision-making.
